notes: The live section, unchanged, caps the whole page at 60. A single fabricated claim caps a section regardless of everything else, and four claims here are contradicted by another page on the same domain — not merely unsourced, but actively refuted one click away. Putting the status inside the badge lifts the cap, because an accurate statement about a future certification is not a false statement about a present one.

Why publish the roadmap at all. A buyer already in conversation, and an assistant asked “is Margo working towards IATF?”, both get a clear answer with a timeframe instead of silence. The bracketed status keeps the two questions separate — what is held today, and what is coming — without ever presenting the second as the first.

Why it is worse than a ranking problem. Per the AI-citation audit, an assistant that finds a certification claimed flatly on one page and denied on another resolves the conflict by dropping the source, not by picking one. That is why every status now reads identically on all four pages that carry one. An overclaim risks silent removal from the answer set — strictly worse than having said nothing.

Schema. Only the ISO 9001:2015 row goes in hasCredential, and only on the homepage Organization node. No In Progress row is emitted as structured data in any form — there is no schema.org property for “certification we are working towards”, and forcing one into hasCredential, award or knowsAbout makes a machine read it as held. In Progress rows are visible text only.

Heading levels.

+ five

card titles. The status bracket is part of the badge

, not the heading — a heading reading “IATF 16949:2016 (In Progress)” puts the caveat into the document outline, where an extraction pass may drop the parenthetical and keep the claim.

Badge images. Do not use ISO or IATF logo marks. Certification body logos are trademark-controlled and their use is licensed by the certificate; a text badge carries the same information with none of the exposure.
Procurement reality. A buyer’s first act after reading this section is to ask for the certificate PDF. Ship the scope and number in the copy so the request confirms rather than contradicts.

fields.label: Q&A ×8
rows: How is a custom rubber part quoted?

Send a drawing, a specification or a physical sample. Margo measures it, identifies the compound family and confirms feasibility, then returns a quotation and feasibility report within 48 hours. Margo produces in bulk against OEM schedules — minimum run from 10,000 pieces per part number, or quoted against the part where size or complexity sets the economics.
Can you manufacture to our drawing?

Yes. Compound, hardness and dimensions are set from your drawing or sample on every one of the eleven product lines. Mould and die tooling is designed and cut in-house from a CAD file, a section drawing or a worn part — no third-party toolroom in the loop.
What if we have no drawing?

Send the physical part. Margo measures it, identifies the compound family and quotes against the sample. A large share of Margo’s work starts as a worn component in an envelope rather than a CAD file, and reverse engineering is a standard route to a first order.
Which rubber material should we specify?

Name the fluid, the operating temperature and the load. Eight compounds are mixed in-house: AEM to 175 °C, FKM to 250 °C, silicone from −60 °C, EPDM for weather and steam, NBR for oil, neoprene, SBR and natural rubber. Margo’s engineers recommend the family at quotation stage.
Do you supply AS568 and metric O-ring series?

Yes. O-rings are supplied to AS568, ISO 3601 and metric series, and to non-standard sections from a drawing. Dimensional conformity is held to ISO 3302-1 classes M1–M4 for moulded parts and E1–E3 for extruded sections; tolerance follows the section.

Quotation within 48 hours of an enquiry. Prototype 48 to 72 hours from an approved drawing, fitment samples inside two weeks, and production in three to four weeks standard or two weeks express. Nhava Sheva is 185 km from the plant, about three hours twenty by road.
Do you provide material certificates and test reports?

Yes. Every despatch lot ships with hardness and dimensional release data, and compound batch, cure parameters and inspection results are retrievable per production batch. APQP and PPAP documentation is provided where the programme requires it. Ozone, fluid immersion and flammability testing goes to a NABL-accredited partner laboratory.
What quality system does Margo operate to?

ISO 9001:2015, certificate 09111526A, issued by Integral Certification Ltd and valid to 21 February 2027. The certified scope covers moulded rubber components, with extension to the extruded and cellular lines in hand. Our quality management system is being upgraded to IATF 16949:2016, with certification targeted by the end of 2026.
